question.text: Which party's member will GPS name as its candidate for Sarawak's Bawang Assan seat before nomination day on 28 November 2026?
question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves according to which party's member is publicly named by Gabungan Parti Sarawak (GPS) as its candidate for the Bawang Assan state seat before 16:00 UTC on 27 November 2026 (00:00 Malaysia time on 28 November 2026, the start of nomination day), as reported by [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions). Select "SUPP" or "PDP" according to the party membership of the person GPS names for Bawang Assan; unilateral statements by a component party that it will field a particular person in Bawang Assan do not count unless they reflect GPS's decision, such as an announcement by GPS chairman Abang Johari Tun Openg or the naming of candidates at the presentation of appointment letters. Timing is set by when GPS's choice was made public, not by when it was first reported, so an announcement made before the cutoff counts even if credible reporting appears afterwards. If no GPS candidate for Bawang Assan had been publicly named by the cutoff, select "No GPS candidate for Bawang Assan publicly named before the cutoff".
question.fine_print: A person's party membership as described in credible reporting at the time of the announcement decides the option, irrespective of earlier party affiliations. If GPS officially names one Bawang Assan candidate and then replaces that person before the cutoff, the most recent official naming before the cutoff decides.

research:
I've finished checking sources. Writing up the findings now.

## 1. Resolution source
- No single official data source decides this. Resolution depends on GPS's own announcement of its line-up, as reported by DayakDaily, Borneo Post, Bernama, The Star and TVS.
- 2026-11-15: Abang Johari said GPS will announce all 82 candidates on **25 November**, three days before nomination day and before the 27 Nov 16:00 UTC cutoff. GPS launches its election machinery on 22 Nov, and he said the list "could change". [The Star](https://www.thestar.com.my/news/nation/2026/11/15/sarawak-polls-gps-to-announce-all-82-candidates-on-nov-25-says-abang-johari); [Newswav](https://newswav.com/article/gps-to-announce-candidates-for-all-82-sarawak-seats-on-nov-25-A2611_4ZkIm6)
- 2026-11-15: A TVS sidebar headline reads "25 November penentu nasib bakal calon GPS" ("25 November decides the fate of GPS hopefuls"). [TVS](https://www.tvsarawak.my/2026/11/15/joshua-ting-sedia-pikul-amanah-di-bawang-assan/)

## 2. Current status
- As of 2026-11-17, I found no report that GPS has named a Bawang Assan candidate. Nothing settles the question yet.
- 2026-11-11: Dr Sim on Bawang Assan: "the Premier will solve it." Abang Johari will issue appointment letters (watikah) after consulting the four component-party presidents. [DayakDaily](https://dayakdaily.com/supp-submits-candidate-list-premier-to-decide-on-batu-lintang-bawang-assan)

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-16: Borneo Post reports that PDP submitted eight names, one for each of its eight seats including Bawang Assan, for Abang Johari's approval. Search snippets did not show whose name it put forward for Bawang Assan, and I could not open the page (HTTP 403). [Borneo Post](https://theborneopost.com/2026/11/16/pdp-submits-eight-names-for-gps-consideration)
- 2026-11-15: Joshua Ting, the Premier's political secretary, said he is ready to contest Bawang Assan "if entrusted by GPS" and that the decision rests entirely with Abang Johari. He cited eight years of local work: five as a Sibu Rural District Council councillor and three as political secretary. [TVS](https://www.tvsarawak.my/2026/11/15/joshua-ting-sedia-pikul-amanah-di-bawang-assan/)
- 2026-11-04: PDP Youth endorsed Ting. DayakDaily describes him as **PDP information chief** and a former PDP Bawang Assan Youth chief. He had breakfast with Wong Soon Koh to discuss "the constituency's way forward". [DayakDaily](https://dayakdaily.com/pdp-youth-back-joshua-ting-for-bawang-assan-seat-in-2026-sarawak-election/)
- 2026-11-03: The Wong-Ting meeting fuelled speculation about a succession. [Borneo Post](https://www.theborneopost.com/2026/11/03/bawang-assan-incumbent-soon-koh-political-secretary-joshua-ting-break-bread-following-succession-rumours/); [FMT](https://www.freemalaysiatoday.com/category/bahasa/tempatan/2026/11/03/pertemuan-dengan-wong-hangat-spekulasi-pdp-tanding-di-bawang-assan)

- 2026-07-04 to 07-06: Dr Sim proposed Kevin Lau. Wong called this an overstep and said the decision is solely the Premier's. [Borneo Post](https://www.theborneopost.com/2026/07/04/dr-sim-proposes-kevin-lau-as-gps-candidate-for-bawang-assan/); [FMT](https://www.freemalaysiatoday.com/category/nation/2026/07/06/wong-slams-immature-gps-colleague-sim-in-seat-dispute)
- 2026-05-16: PDP president Tiong King Sing said PDP will defend all eight seats it holds, Bawang Assan among them. [Malay Mail](https://www.malaymail.com/news/malaysia/2026/05/16/pdp-to-defend-all-eight-seats-in-next-sarawak-state-polls-says-tiong-king-sing/220217)
- 2024-06-01: Analysts expected SUPP to win the dispute. [FMT](https://www.freemalaysiatoday.com/category/nation/2024/06/01/supp-likely-to-prevail-in-spat-over-soon-kohs-seat-say-analysts)

**Caveat on Ting's party:** He is a PDP office-holder but also the Premier's aide. The Premier is PBB president, and a 2019 PBB figure (Romeo) was also linked to the seat. Under the fine print, his party label in reporting on the day of the announcement decides the option. Current reporting labels him PDP.

## 4. Base rates
- 2021: GPS released its full 82-candidate list two days before nomination and named a candidate for every seat. [DayakDaily](https://dayakdaily.com/gps-candidate-list-for-12th-sarawak-election-to-be-released-2-days-before-nomination-day) GPS has always fielded in every seat, so "no candidate named" would be historically unusual.
- 2016 precedent: BN settled the SUPP-UPP seat dispute by fielding "direct BN" candidates, Wong in Bawang Assan among them. So creative compromises have happened before. I found no sign of a "direct GPS" mechanism this time.
- Seats inherited from other parties: PDP took over Bawang Assan, Engkilili and Ba'kelalan from the dissolved PSB. I found no announced outcome yet for Engkilili, which could serve as a parallel.

## 5. Other forecasts
- No Polymarket, Kalshi, Manifold or Metaculus market covers Bawang Assan. The Kalshi market on GPS's seat total (e.g. "78 or more" at 0.60) does not match this question.
- 2024 analysts favoured SUPP (see above). I found no recent expert forecast.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- 2026-11-22: GPS machinery launch, where hints are possible.
- **2026-11-25: GPS announces all 82 candidates**, likely together with the watikah presentation. This is the key event.
- 2026-11-27 16:00 UTC: Cutoff. A last-minute replacement before then would count.
- 2026-11-28: Nomination day, after the cutoff.
- Risk to watch: if the Bawang Assan pick is held back past 25 Nov (as Batu Lintang also was), it could slip close to the cutoff.

## 4. Base rates
- 2021: GPS published its full list two days before nomination day. This time the announcement is set for three days before. GPS met its own announcement schedule in 2021, which suggests a pick will almost certainly be public before the cutoff. [DayakDaily](https://dayakdaily.com/gps-candidate-list-for-12th-sarawak-election-to-be-released-2-days-before-nomination-day)
- 2021, from my own memory and not checked this session: GPS gave Dudong, traditionally a SUPP seat, to PDP's Tiong King Sing. That is a precedent for handing a SUPP seat in Sibu to PDP.
- 2021: analysts expected GPS to field "direct candidates" in Sibu seats where components had overlapping claims. BN used this approach in 2016, including for Wong himself. [Malay Mail](https://www.malaymail.com/news/malaysia/2021/11/30/sarawak-polls-analysts-believe-gps-will-field-direct-candidates-as-componen/2024848)
- 2024: PBB's Bawang Assan branch chief said PBB would back SUPP for the seat "as advised by Abang Johari," and analysts then expected SUPP to win the dispute. [FMT](https://www.freemalaysiatoday.com/category/nation/2024/06/01/supp-likely-to-prevail-in-spat-over-soon-kohs-seat-say-analysts), [Borneo Post](https://www.theborneopost.com/2024/05/03/pdp-man-chides-pbb-branch-chairman-for-pledging-support-to-supp-in-bawang-assan/)
- Signals for each side:
  - **PDP:** it holds the seat through Wong, PDP's candidate is the Premier's own political secretary, and there is the Dudong precedent.
  - **SUPP:** five terms holding the seat in the past, the 2024 signals above, and its "recapture" push.
- I found nothing pointing to a PBB or PRS candidate, or to a non-member.

## 5. Other forecasts
- No prediction market or expert forecast exists for this seat.
- The Kalshi market on GPS's total seat count (for example, 78 or more seats at 0.60) is related but does not address which party gets Bawang Assan.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution

- 2026-11-25: GPS announces all 82 candidates. This is the most likely point of resolution.
- 2026-11-27, 16:00 UTC: cutoff. Nomination day is 28 November.
- Risks to watch:
  - The announcement slips past the cutoff (this looks unlikely).
  - A "direct candidate" or compromise pick.
  - A fallout, such as Wong or the losing party's man running as an independent, which would not change who GPS named.
  - The question of whether Joshua Ting is still a PDP member when he is named.

forecasts.reasoning:
(a) **Time left:** About 10 days. GPS says it will announce all 82 candidates on 25 November. The cutoff is 27 November at 16:00 UTC.

(b) **Status quo:** No GPS candidate is named yet. The seat is held by a PDP incumbent, Wong Soon Koh. If GPS follows its usual practice of giving a seat to the party of the sitting assemblyman, the default pick is PDP.

(c) **Base rates:**
- In 2021 GPS named candidates for all seats about two days before nomination day. A "no candidate named" outcome is therefore rare, maybe 5% after allowing for delays.
- Seat disputes in BN/GPS were usually settled in favour of the incumbent's party, or through compromise devices such as "direct BN" candidates in 2016.
- Analysts in 2024 expected SUPP to prevail on the "traditional seat" argument.
- Together this suggests a starting point of roughly 50/40 PDP vs SUPP.

(d) **Strongest evidence:**
- 15 November: Joshua Ting, PDP information chief and also the Premier's own political secretary, publicly said he is ready to contest "if entrusted by GPS." TVS gave this prominent coverage.
- 4 November: PDP Youth endorsed Ting.
- 3 November: Ting met Wong Soon Koh, fuelling "succession" talk.
- Lumi News headline: "Abang Johari's aide tipped for Bawang Assan seat."
- 16 November: PDP submitted eight names, including one for Bawang Assan.
- 16 May: Tiong King Sing said PDP will defend all eight of its seats.
- 11 November: SUPP left Bawang Assan for the Premier to decide rather than insisting on it, which suggests it may be preparing to concede.
- Abang Johari alone decides. A candidate who is both his aide and a PDP member neatly answers SUPP's objection to Wong.

On this evidence I move from about 50% to about 60% for PDP.

(e) **Unexpected outcome:** Abang Johari could give Bawang Assan to SUPP's Kevin Lau to keep the Chinese-majority seat balance, and compensate PDP elsewhere. Alternatively he could field Ting under a PBB label or as a direct GPS candidate. A further possibility is that the Bawang Assan decision is held back beyond 25 November and slips past the cutoff.

Option_A: 0.30
Option_B: 0.58
Option_C: 0.06
Option_D: 0.06

(a) **Time left:** about 10 days. GPS says it will announce all 82 candidates on 25 November. The cutoff is 27 November, 16:00 UTC, so the answer should be public within 8 to 10 days.

(b) **Status quo:** No GPS candidate for Bawang Assan has been named yet. The seat is held by Wong Soon Koh, who is now in PDP. If GPS follows its usual practice of naming a full slate before nomination day, the "none named" outcome is unlikely. The default holder of the seat on incumbency grounds is PDP.

(c) **Base rates:**
- GPS and BN in Sarawak have always named a full slate before nomination. In 2021 GPS released its list two days before nomination.
- When seat disputes arise, the incumbent's party usually keeps the seat, especially when the incumbent defected into the coalition. The alternative is a creative compromise, such as the "direct BN" candidates of 2016.
- The legacy-seat claim (SUPP) sometimes wins, but less often than incumbency.
- My prior is about 55 to 60% that PDP keeps the seat, about 30% that SUPP gets it, and a small remainder for the other options.

(d) **Strongest evidence:**
- **PDP's defence:** PDP president Tiong said on 16 May that PDP would defend all eight of its seats. On 16 November PDP submitted eight names, including one for Bawang Assan.
- **Joshua Ting:** Ting is PDP information chief and also the Premier's own political secretary.
  - On 3 November he met Wong amid succession rumours, and on 4 November PDP Youth endorsed him.
  - On 15 November TVS ran a profile of him saying he is ready to contest.
  - A Lumi headline says "Abang Johari's aide tipped for Bawang Assan".
  - A candidate who is close to the Premier gives Abang Johari a face-saving compromise: the seat stays with PDP, but the candidate is his own aide.
- **SUPP's push:** On 4 July Dr Sim proposed Kevin Lau. On 11 November SUPP left Bawang Assan for the Premier to decide rather than conceding it. Analysts in 2024 favoured SUPP.
- **Timing:** Abang Johari said the full list of 82 candidates comes on 25 November, before the cutoff.

(e) **Unexpected scenarios:**
- Abang Johari could field a candidate from his own party, PBB, as a neutral compromise, or relabel Ting.
- He could hold Bawang Assan back, as might also happen with Batu Lintang, and name the candidate only at the watikah ceremony on nomination eve, after the cutoff.
- He could hand the seat to SUPP in exchange for giving Batu Lintang to someone else.

**Adjustment from the prior:** I moved PDP up slightly from my prior because of the Ting signals. The Premier's own aide is being publicly profiled by state broadcaster TVS. I kept SUPP's chances meaningful because the seat is still openly contested and Abang Johari has said the list "could change".

Option_B: 0.58
Option_C: 0.06
Option_D: 0.07

**(a) Time left:** About 10 days until the cutoff (27 Nov, 16:00 UTC). The key event is GPS's announced release of all 82 candidates on 25 November.

**(b) Status quo:** No GPS candidate has been named yet. The incumbent, Wong Soon Koh, is now a PDP member, and PDP has formally submitted a name for Bawang Assan. If GPS follows its usual incumbency norm, the seat stays with PDP.

**(c) Base rates:**
- GPS and BN have always fielded candidates in every seat and released their lists before nomination day. That makes "no candidate named" rare, perhaps under 5%, since the list is due 25 Nov.
- Within GPS, incumbency usually decides seat ownership, which favours PDP.
- Disputes involving a "traditional" seat claim have sometimes gone the other way, for example the 2016 direct-BN compromise. In 2024, analysts expected SUPP to prevail.
- A rough prior is PDP 50%, SUPP 40%, other 5%, none 5%.

**(d) Strongest evidence:**
- **15 Nov:** Abang Johari set 25 Nov to announce all 82 candidates, which is before the cutoff.
- **15 Nov:** State broadcaster TVS ran a profile of Joshua Ting, who said he is ready "if entrusted by GPS."
- **4 Nov:** PDP Youth endorsed Ting. He is both PDP information chief and the Premier's own political secretary.
- **3 Nov:** Ting met Wong Soon Koh over breakfast, which reporters framed as a succession signal.
- **Undated:** A Lumi News headline reads "Abang Johari's aide tipped for Bawang Assan seat."
- **16 Nov:** PDP submitted eight names, including one for Bawang Assan.
- **11 Nov:** SUPP left the Bawang Assan decision to the Premier rather than insisting on it.
